## The Content Creation Dataset

Throughout these lectures we will use a sample of **346 short-form videos** posted on YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram Reels. For each video, the dataset records:

- **Categorical variables:** platform, topic, video format, thumbnail style, production effort, posting day, posting time, and whether paid promotion was used.
- **Quantitative variables:** creator audience size, creator tenure, posting frequency, video length, title length, impressions, views, watch time, percentage viewed, likes, comments, shares, and subscribers gained.

There are no missing values. The dataset is a sample, so we will use it to learn about the larger population of short-form videos.

## Definitions: Populations and Samples

::: {.callout title="Definitions"}
**Statistics** is the field concerned with collecting, organizing, analyzing, and drawing conclusions from data.

A **population** is the complete collection of all objects or measurements of interest.

A **sample** is a subset of data selected from a population.

A **parameter** is a numerical summary of a population. Parameters are often denoted by Greek letters, such as $\mu$ for a population mean and $p$ for a population proportion.

A **statistic** is a numerical summary computed from a sample. Statistics are often denoted by Latin letters, such as $\bar{x}$ for a sample mean and $\hat{p}$ for a sample proportion.
:::

## Example: Average Views

Suppose we want to study the average number of first-week views for all short-form videos posted on YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram Reels. We collect data on 346 videos and compute the average number of first-week views for those 346 videos.

- The **population** is all short-form videos posted on these three platforms.
- The **sample** is the 346 videos in our dataset.
- The **parameter** is the average first-week views for all videos in the population, denoted $\mu$.
- The **statistic** is the average first-week views for the 346 sampled videos, denoted $\bar{x}$.

## Example: Paid Promotion

Suppose we want to know what proportion of all short-form videos use paid promotion. In our sample, 35 of the 346 videos used paid promotion, so the sample proportion is $35/346 \approx 0.101$.

- The **population** is all short-form videos posted on these three platforms.
- The **sample** is the 346 videos in our dataset.
- The **parameter** is the proportion of all videos in the population that use paid promotion, denoted $p$.
- The **statistic** is the proportion of sampled videos that use paid promotion, denoted $\hat{p} \approx 0.101$.

## Practice: Average Watch Time

A marketing team wants to study the average first-week watch time for all short-form videos on these platforms. They collect the 346 videos in our dataset and compute the average watch time of those videos.

Identify the population, sample, population parameter, and sample statistic, including the appropriate symbols.

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout title="Solution"}
- **Population:** all short-form videos posted on YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram Reels.
- **Sample:** the 346 videos in the dataset.
- **Parameter:** the average first-week watch time for all videos in the population, denoted $\mu$.
- **Statistic:** the average first-week watch time for the 346 sampled videos, denoted $\bar{x}$.
:::
:::

## Definitions: Descriptive Statistics and Inference

::: {.callout title="Definitions"}
**Descriptive statistics** organize, describe, summarize, and display data.

**Statistical inference** is an estimate, prediction, decision, or generalization about a population based on information from a sample.
:::

## Example: Describing the Sample

An analyst reports that the average first-week watch time in the sample of 346 videos is about **21.1 seconds** and that the median is **18 seconds**.

This is an example of **descriptive statistics**. The analyst is summarizing the sample and is not making a claim about all short-form videos.

## Example: Generalizing Beyond the Sample

An analyst finds that **10.1%** of the sampled videos used paid promotion and concludes that roughly **10% of all short-form videos on these platforms** use paid promotion.

This is an example of **statistical inference**. The analyst uses a sample statistic to make a generalization about the population.

## Practice: Descriptive or Inferential?

A researcher finds that 95% of the sampled videos have an average percentage viewed between 5% and 20%, then concludes that the average percentage viewed for all short-form videos on these platforms is likely between 5% and 20%.

Is this descriptive statistics or statistical inference?

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout title="Solution"}
This is **statistical inference**. The researcher uses a summary of the sample to make a claim about the entire population of short-form videos.
:::
:::
